reason: The text includes several regular people characters who demonstrate meaningful agency. Most notably, the 'people of the land' (כָל־עַם־הָאָרֶץ) actively participate in key events: they rejoice at the coronation of Joash, and most significantly, they collectively act to destroy the Baal temple—'all the people of the land came to the house of Baal and tore it down, its altars and its images they broke thoroughly.' The military captains and guards also show agency in their covenant-taking, oath-swearing, and strategic positioning to protect the new king. While the narrative is dominated by elite figures (Jehoiada the priest, Jehosheba the princess, and Athaliah the queen), the lower-status military leaders and common population are portrayed as volitional agents who make choices and take actions that affect the story's outcome.
